chapter: Tenor players, tours and band boys
title: New York versus California and why New York is unique
summary: Francis argues New York offers studios, theatres, club dates and jazz clubs, whereas California depends on studios; he calls New York America.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's one of the great things about New York; a man that is qualified in New York can take his pick and go through all these different phases -- that is one of the great things that most people really don't realize about New York. We had the Broadway shows, we have a tremendous amount of hotels.

It's the only place that you have the variety of playing different music and can still make a decent living. See, like out in California, if you're not in the studios, forget it. Because club dates don't pay any money in California, you know? I don't know about the theatres, because I mean, I haven't been there lately ...
Well, you know that Broadway has got the theatres; we know that.
But everything in California depends on the studios, whereas in New York, you have the studios, you have the theatres, you have the club dates --
And you got the jazz clubs; if you want to pay jazz only, you can make a living at it, you know?

And I really find -- you know, I get into quite a few arguments with people about New York City, because to me, I have traveled like three quarters around the world, and I've been to Paris and London - and all these are great cities.
I mean I really like all these towns, but New York is unique.
: Thank you for speaking so well of the Apple, because I came there to die.

Well, but it's so unique, you know? It's the only place in the world that you can find every nationality and every type of food that you want to eat, you can find it in New York. I know of no other place where you can do that; in fact, I tell people that New York IS America. Because everything you find in the rest of America, you're gonna find it in New York.
